source.title: Safe Delta: Consistently Preserving Safety when Fine-Tuning LLMs on Diverse Datasets
source.authors: Ning Lu; Sheng-Cai Liu; Jiahao Wu; Wei-Yu Chen; Zhi-Rui Zhang; Y. Ong; Qi Wang; Ke Tang

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes aligned chat models on harmful and benign datasets and measures harmful-request safety using attack success rate, directly testing the fine-tuning effect with the same general intervention and measure as the original work.
record.gate_note: The raw fine-tuned-model results directly test harmful and benign fine-tuning effects. The paper also reports defense-method comparisons, but those results assess methods such as Safe Delta rather than testing the first-token, parameter-localization, or shallowness claims. The appendix's GPT-4 evaluation prompt is an evaluation prompt, not an instruction to this reader.
record.test_reason: Primarily a defense paper (Safe Delta), but it reports its own undefended fine-tuning results. These use Qi et al.'s PureBad, Identity Shift and Dirty Summary datasets plus GSM8k. They are measured with the same Policy-Oriented benchmark, keyword ASR and GPT-4 harmfulness score as the original. The fine-tuned-model baselines bear directly on V1 and V2. The transfer-jailbreak table bears only weakly on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors take fine-tuning-induced safety degradation, from harmful or benign data, as given from prior work and show it in their baselines. Their conclusion is that Safe Delta preserves safety while retaining utility across dataset types, sizes and models, outperforming existing defenses.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses harmful fine-tuning datasets and a refusal-based ASR safety evaluation, including datasets and benchmarks associated with the original work, but its focus is evaluating a new defense across additional datasets and models rather than an explicitly named replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The safety effect varies by fine-tuning dataset and model: harmful datasets produce very high ASR, Dirty Summary also raises ASR, and clean Math produces a smaller increase. The paper also reports results at multiple PureBad dataset sizes.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the safety-behaviour results. ASR is computed using a predefined refusal-keyword list, and safety evaluation uses 330 benchmark questions; the text does not report validation of the keyword-based refusal measure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional raw fine-tuning safety results relevant to the tested versions were omitted. Defense comparisons and Safe Delta ablations were not catalogued as fine-tuning-effect results; Table 9 repeats the Llama-3 results already shown in Table 4.

untested.parts: Models other than Llama-2-7B/13B-chat and Llama-3-8B-instruct; closed models.
Only one clean benign dataset (GSM8k Math), on Llama-2-7B-Chat only. No Alpaca/Dolly-style benign sets, and no 'carefully chosen' benign data.
Not tested: no per-token KL or position analysis.
Prefilling, decoding changes, and white-box GCG on the target model are not tested; only transfer attacks are.
Not tested; Safe Delta selects delta parameters but does not test localization of safety.
Not tested; Safe Delta is a post-hoc weight edit, not deepening training.

missing.what: Fine-tuned model ASR on PureBad and Identity Shift at harmful dataset sizes 50, 100, 150 and 200 (undefended curve)

After Llama-Guard filtering removed 83% of PureBad, fine-tuning on the remaining ~17 harmful examples still gave ASR 82.1%. Filtered Dirty Summary gave 51.7%; AOA gave 88.5% and Math 11.5%, both unfiltered.
LoRA (rank 8, q/k) fine-tuning on PureBad and Dirty Summary: per-category harmfulness scores of the fine-tuned model versus the original

record.verdict_notes: Dirty Summary was misassigned to V2; it contains 100 PureBad examples and is reassigned to V1. Defense-method rows for V4 are removed. V4 evidence is limited to one transfer-GCG number, and the model for Tables 10 and 12 is not named. ASR uses a refusal keyword list that includes 'illegal' and 'unethical', which may undercount compliance. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests datasets of 100 examples and, in an additional experiment, 1k and 10k examples; it does not test every size in the claim's range.
Benign fine-tuning is tested on Dirty Summary, which includes 100 harmful examples, and on Math; other benign datasets are not tested.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurements or response-position analysis.

The study tests GCG, AutoDAN, and PAIR jailbreak attacks on the original model and a PureBad-fine-tuned model with Safe Delta. It does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes, and it does not isolate the effect of suffixes.
The method selects and compensates delta parameters, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
No test of whether the data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Safe Delta is a post-fine-tuning defense, not a test of training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.
